recentActivity.message:
docs: fix cost-reduction number presentation; add engineering judgment doc

Presentation-only pass (no analysis logic changed, no pipelines re-run) ahead of putting the
portfolio on a resume/site:

- Both dashboards (top-level portfolio_dashboard.html and forecastiq's own forecast_dashboard.html)
  now lead with ForecastIQ's fair-baseline cost-reduction number (78%) as the headline stat, with
  the weak all-time-average baseline (89.8%) demoted to second position and explicitly labeled
  "weak baseline, inflated" rather than appearing unqualified alongside it. Matched precision
  (one decimal place) so both dashboards report the same 89.8% for that stat.
- Added docs/engineering_judgment.md: nine chronological items (bugs caught, models cross-checked
  against a dumb baseline on purpose, an overclaim corrected, negative results reported honestly)
  pulled from the three project READMEs, each closing on a bolded general principle.
- Linked it prominently from the top-level README, right under the headline results table, and
  added a "Bugs caught, baselines corrected" card to the top of the portfolio dashboard pulling
  four one-line highlights from the doc.

Verified: zero remaining unqualified "89.8%"/"90%" occurrences repo-wide, both dashboards rebuild
cleanly by re-reading their existing analysis_results.json (no re-analysis), full test suite and
ruff still green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: repo-wide quality pass — error handling, config discipline, tests, dedup, tooling

Follows a full-repo improvement audit (3 parallel explore passes) turned into a 6-phase plan:

- Fix stale/misleading docs: generate.py's "skeleton" docstring, architecture.md's premature
  Dockerfile claims.
- Add error handling at I/O boundaries: config validation in shopsphere-data/generate.py,
  missing-data checks in experimentiq/data.py, a wrapped 500 in modelguard/api.py's predict().
- Move ~10 hardcoded generator/analysis values into YAML config (orders/events/inventory
  distributions, forecastiq's naive-baseline trailing window, modelguard's risk-band cutoffs and
  classification threshold), matching the repo's own "config via YAML" rule.
- Add missing test coverage: shopsphere-data's generate.py orchestrator, shared/'s style and
  constants modules, uplift.py::build_features, and a real HTTP-layer TestClient suite for the
  ModelGuard API (including the 503 model-not-loaded path).
- Extract real, unexploited duplication into shared/: shared/cli.py for the three
  run_analysis.py scripts' argparse/config-load/write-results boilerplate, and
  DASHBOARD_BASE_CSS for the three project dashboards' identical stylesheet block.
- Add tooling: ruff configured (E/F/I, no E501) and the repo made clean, a requirements-lock.txt
  pinning the exact tested environment, a documented root-level `pytest` command, and
  forecastiq's blanket warning suppression narrowed to the one thing it was actually hiding.

Every generator/analysis change was verified value-preserving: regenerated data and all three
projects' analysis_results.json/dashboards were diffed against committed versions (byte-identical
or differing only in expected non-substantive ways — MLflow's model_version bump, one
floating-point noise digit, CSS whitespace) before being reverted, so no regenerated artifact is
part of this commit. Full suite: 116 passed, ruff clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: stop tracking an internal notes file; make README self-contained

Removed an internal session-continuity file from git tracking (still present
on disk locally, now gitignored) -- it wasn't meant for the public repo
browse view. History isn't rewritten, so it remains recoverable from earlier
commits if ever needed; nothing in it was sensitive.

Rewrote README.md so it no longer depends on that file for context: each
project now gets its real business question, method, and headline result
directly in the README, plus an engineering-approach section. It should now
read cold, with no other file required.

docs: fix broken dev-instructions link, add demo screenshots

README's closing line pointed at a project instructions file that's
intentionally excluded from the repo -- broken link for anyone viewing
on GitHub. Replaced with a link to the already-tracked
dev/active/chess-tutor/ directory.

Also adds a short Demo section with two real screenshots: Manual FEN
mode (move-checker + FEN-similarity retrieval) and the Game 4
low-confidence hedge.

docs: note has_open_review_flags conflates confirmed disputes with unclosed audit samples

engine_verify_mismatch/pgn_lookup_mismatch (something actually found wrong) and
engine_verify_sample_review (randomly selected for audit, nothing found wrong yet)
both set has_open_review_flags=True and trigger identical hedge language today.
Found while investigating why a clean text-only query about Example 1 (Rook+King
checkmate) still produced a hedge -- traced to two genuinely flagged passages
(Example 59, a real engine-verify mismatch; Example 2, just an unclosed audit
sample) among the 8 retrieved chunks, not a bug in the hedge mechanism itself.

feat: multi-modal RAG + LangGraph agentic chess tutor

Ingests José Capablanca's public-domain 1921 book *Chess Fundamentals* into an
enriched knowledge base (prose + vision-extracted FEN + verified PGN per
example/game), then serves a 4-agent LangGraph pipeline (position classifier,
deterministic hybrid+FEN-similarity retriever, move/plan checker, coach) that
visibly hedges on any content the ingestion pipeline couldn't fully verify.

- ingestion/: PDF segmentation, diagram detection, Gemini vision FEN extraction
  with 3-layer validation, PGN-database move sourcing (Stockfish verification
  for tactical examples, LLM notation parsing as a last-resort fallback),
  theme/imbalance tagging, Chroma load
- retrieval/: hybrid (semantic + BM25 + cross-encoder rerank) + FEN-similarity
  retrieval, merged and deduped
- agents/ + graph/: 4-agent LangGraph workflow with conditional routing
- api/: FastAPI backend (ask, extract-fen, diagrams, review-queue)
- frontend/: Streamlit chat UI, image-upload HITL flow, review-queue browser
- eval/: RAGAS-based evaluation harness + FEN-extraction accuracy report +
  per-question Faithfulness re-scoring tool
- docs/limitations.md + README.md: honest, numbers-backed account of what's
  verified, what's flagged, and what's unresolved
- tests/: 318 tests (2 integration, need real API keys)

See dev/active/chess-tutor/{plan,context,tasks}.md for the full plan, decision
log, and phase-by-phase build history.
